mauritshuis.name: Mauritshuis
mauritshuis.slogan: A small palace with the world's most famous turban.
mauritshuis.line: Built 1636-1641 for John Maurice of Nassau, it now holds Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring and Fabritius's The Goldfinch.

hofvijver.name: Binnenhof and Hofvijver
hofvijver.slogan: Dutch politics, mirrored in a court pond.
hofvijver.line: The Binnenhof grew from a hunting lodge bought by Count Floris IV in 1229; the prime minister's office has sat in the little Torentje since 1982.

vredespaleis.name: Peace Palace
vredespaleis.slogan: Where nations take their disputes to court instead of to war.
vredespaleis.line: Opened in 1913 with US$1.5 million from Andrew Carnegie; the design by Cordonnier beat 215 other entries.

kunstmuseum.name: Kunstmuseum Den Haag
kunstmuseum.slogan: Mondrian's last, loudest grid, in Berlage's brick.
kunstmuseum.line: Berlage's building opened in 1935 and holds the largest Mondrian collection in the world, including Victory Boogie Woogie.

kurhaus.name: Kurhaus Scheveningen
kurhaus.slogan: A grand 1885 seaside salon with the North Sea at its door.
kurhaus.line: The Rolling Stones played here in 1964 and had to flee the building to escape the crowd of fans.
